ow1.title: EO 14154 / BOEM COP Approval Freeze
ow1.subtitle: Two stacked executive instruments now control the lease and COP approval pipeline. The administration's playbook is delay-by-process, not formal denial.
ow1.view: Two stacked executive instruments — the Jan 20, 2025 OCSLA §12(a) withdrawal memorandum and Executive Order 14154 — give the administration plenary withdrawal authority over unleased OCS and direct every reviewing agency to slow-walk anything that 'subsidizes' offshore wind. The slow-walk operates through BOEM §585.628 disapproval discretion, supplemental EIS triggers, USACE §10/§404 timing, and NMFS take authorizations. The Empire Wind 1 stop-work in April 2025 proved mid-construction halt is a live tool. Base rate from Vineyard Wind 1's 2019–21 pause: 12–24 months of recoverable delay — 3–6% of capex per six months for a project late in development. We hold the 18-month probability of continued de facto COP freeze at 78%, with mid-construction stop-work episode at 43% conditional on at least one major project advancing.

ow3.title: Section 232 Steel on Monopile / Tower Plate
ow3.subtitle: 50% global ad valorem on HTS 7208.51 plate. No country exclusions. No active BIS product-exclusion process.
ow3.view: Proclamation 10896 (Feb 10, 2025) re-imposed the 25% §232 steel tariff globally and terminated every country-specific exemption and the BIS product-exclusion process. Trade-press signals indicate a doubling to 50% in mid-2025 — we treat 50% as the operating rate on HTS 7208.51 plate. A 14 MW monopile carries 1,500–2,500 mt of >50mm plate; at ~$1,500/ton landed pre-tariff, a 50% duty adds $1.1–1.9M per monopile. For an 800 MW project (~57 monopiles): $65–110M tariff incidence on foundations, plus $15–20M tower steel. EEW Paulsboro is the only US monopile fabricator at scale and well below campaign-year requirement; redesigning to <50mm plate is the principal mitigation. Probability the tariff stays at ≥50% on relevant HTS lines through Nov 2027: 90%. Probability of upward expansion (>50% or new derivatives): 32%.

ow5.title: §45Y / §48E Narrowing for Offshore Wind
ow5.subtitle: OBBBA narrowing landed hard on offshore wind. Treasury offshore-specific guidance remains in proposed form.
ow5.view: OBBBA reconciliation in 2025 narrowed §45Y/§48E for projects without locked-in begin-of-construction status; offshore wind has been treated harshly relative to onshore/solar because of perceived European supply-chain alignment. Treasury's offshore-specific domestic-content table (Notice 2024-41) is still in proposed form — finalization or withdrawal is the next high-information event. For an 800 MW project (~$4B capex, 38% capacity factor) the base §48E ITC at 30% PWA-met is ~$1.0B PV; the full 40% with domestic-content bonus is ~$1.35B PV. Material narrowing (FEOC tightening, BOC cutoff acceleration, transferability narrowing) is the high-probability mode — we price 70% over 18 months. Full retroactive repeal sits in the 5–10% tail; Takings-Clause exposure is the floor.

ow7.title: NEPA / ESA / NMFS — Right Whale Channel
ow7.subtitle: Post-Seven County, the scope of NEPA review narrowed. The administration's lever is ITA delay, not denial.
ow7.view: Three statutory channels converge: NEPA EIS for COP approval, ESA §7 consultation (right whale, ~370 individuals, critically endangered), and MMPA §101(a)(5) ITA/IHA for site characterization and pile driving. Post-*Seven County Infrastructure* (S.Ct. 2024) the scope of NEPA effects review narrowed favorably to defendants. NMFS ITA cadence dropped sharply in 2025–26 — the dominant risk vector is now delay, not denial. Probability at least one NEPA challenge is filed against a major COP/ROD in 18 months: 78%. Probability of an injunction or vacatur: 14%. Standard challenge denied at district court costs ~$10–40M; full vacatur with remand for supplemental EIS = 8–20% of capex.
